relationships.description: The communication path is bound to a specific technology interface endpoint, so the traffic it carries terminates at that listening port, socket or broker listener.
relationships.evidence: A connection string, firewall rule or service-mesh route for the link names the interface's host and port (e.g. db.internal:5432) as its endpoint.

relationships.description: An end-to-end communication path is built from constituent path segments, such as hops or tunnel legs, that exist only as parts of that overall link.
relationships.evidence: Network topology documentation or Terraform defines a site-to-site VPN connection whose tunnel resources or peering hops are declared as sub-components of that single connection.

relationships.description: Data exchanged over the communication path is delivered to the technology service at its far end, such as requests carried to a database or messaging capability.
relationships.evidence: Traffic flow diagrams, network policies or mesh telemetry show requests travelling over the link and arriving at the service's endpoint (e.g. a NetworkPolicy allowing egress to the database service).

relationships.description: The communication path itself is the concrete mechanism that delivers a connectivity-type technology service, such as a managed VPN, private link or message channel offered to consumers.
relationships.evidence: A service catalog entry or Terraform module for a connectivity offering (e.g. a private-link or VPN service) is implemented by provisioning this specific tunnel or channel resource.

relationships.description: The communication path provides connectivity to a physical device, letting that hardware exchange data with the other endpoints on the link.
relationships.evidence: Network inventory or switch/router configuration lists the device's port or IP as an endpoint of the VLAN, circuit or tunnel.

relationships.description: The communication path provides connectivity to a hosting node, such as a VM, container or cluster, enabling the workloads on it to reach other endpoints.
relationships.evidence: Infrastructure-as-code attaches the node to the link, e.g. a subnet route, security group rule or VPC peering entry referencing the VM or cluster, or a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy selecting its pods.

relationships.description: A state change on the communication path, such as the link going down, a tunnel renegotiating or latency exceeding a threshold, raises a discrete technology event.
relationships.evidence: Monitoring configuration defines an alert or health-check rule on the link (e.g. a CloudWatch alarm on VPN TunnelState or a connection-probe failure) that emits the named event.

notes: flows-to and realizes toward TechnologyService overlap ambiguously. A path usually serves or carries traffic to a service rather than realizing it, and realizes fits only connectivity services. serves toward Device and Node is the same notion split by target type. ArchiMate models a path as associated-with its nodes rather than serving them.
